# Stable isotope labeling and flux analysis {#sec-stable-isotope-labeling}

::: {.callout-note}
## What you should know before reading this chapter

This chapter builds on [Metabolomics](../metabolomics/index.qmd) and assumes you are comfortable with the following.

- Feature detection and metabolite annotation, as covered in @sec-feature-detection and @sec-annotation.
- Isotopes, isotopologues, and how they appear in a mass spectrum.
- Basic linear algebra, specifically matrix notation and solving linear systems.
- Elementary knowledge of central carbon metabolism and of what a metabolic pathway is.

<!-- TODO: add links to external resources for each prerequisite. -->

The flux analysis sections assume more quantitative background than the rest of the book.
Readers from a wetlab background may prefer to read @sec-labeling-strategies first and return to @sec-flux-calculations afterwards.
:::

This part covers how isotopically labeled tracers turn a metabolomics measurement into a statement about metabolic activity.

- @sec-labeling-strategies covers experimental design, tracer choice, and getting from raw data to a corrected labeling pattern.
- @sec-flux-calculations covers turning those patterns into flux estimates, and how much to trust them.
